definitions.gloss: higan service; Buddhist memorial service held during the spring and autumn equinoxes
definitions.explanation: A Buddhist ceremony held during the week centered on the spring equinox (around March 20) and autumn equinox (around September 23). Families visit graves, make offerings, and hold memorial services for the deceased during this period.

examples.japanese: {彼岸会|ひがんえ}に{参加|さんか}する。
examples.english: To attend a higan memorial service.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}の{彼岸会|ひがんえ}で{先祖|せんぞ}の{供養|くよう}をした。
examples.english: We held a memorial offering for our ancestors at the spring higan service.

examples.japanese: {菩提寺|ぼだいじ}の{彼岸会|ひがんえ}に{家族|かぞく}{全員|ぜんいん}で{出席|しゅっせき}し、{住職|じゅうしょく}の{法話|ほうわ}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: The whole family attended the higan service at our family temple and listened to the head priest's sermon.

notes:
Compound of {彼岸|ひがん} ('the other shore; higan period') and {会|え} ('gathering; meeting'). The word {彼岸|ひがん} originally refers to the Buddhist concept of the 'other shore' — enlightenment or the afterlife — and the equinox periods are traditionally believed to be times when the worlds of the living and dead are closest.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The higan period lasts seven days: the equinox itself plus three days before and after. During this time, many Japanese families visit cemeteries, clean gravestones, and leave offerings such as flowers and おはぎ (rice cakes coated in sweet red bean paste). Temples hold formal {彼岸会|ひがんえ} services with chanting and sermons.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {春|はる}の{彼岸会|ひがんえ}: spring higan service
- {秋|あき}の{彼岸会|ひがんえ}: autumn higan service
- {彼岸会|ひがんえ}の{法要|ほうよう}: higan religious ceremony
- {彼岸会|ひがんえ}に{参列|さんれつ}する: to attend a higan service

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {彼岸|ひがん}: higan period; the equinox season — the broader period, not specifically the service
- {法要|ほうよう}: Buddhist memorial service — a general term for any Buddhist ceremony; not limited to higan
- お{盆|ぼん}: Bon festival — the midsummer festival for honoring the dead; a separate observance from higan
- {供養|くよう}: memorial offering — the act of making offerings for the dead; performed during higan and other occasions
